blocks.text: Zero Trust Branch forwarding policies provide a secure, scalable, and highly available framework for branch network traffic, enabling you to control traffic from branch sites to specific destinations.

blocks.item: From the navigation menu, go to Zero Trust Branch > Deployments > Sites.
On the Sites page, locate and click the name of the site in the Site column.
See image.
On the site details page, click the Forwarding Policy tab and then click Configure.
See image.
Click Add Forwarding Rule.
See image.
The Add Forwarding Rule drawer appears.
In the Add Forwarding Rule drawer:
Rule Name: Enter a name for the forwarding rule.

Sources: Select the sources to which the forwarding rule must apply from the drop-down menu. Sources can include one or more networks, MAC addresses, devices, and Active Directory (AD) users. Select the Negate checkbox if you want the policy to apply to all sources except the ones selected.
Add CIDR: Enter the IP address range in CIDR format for the selected sources. This option appears only if the Subnet/host type source is selected.

Destinations: Select the destinations to which the forwarding rule must apply from the drop-down menu. Destinations can include one or more networks, devices, domains, AD users, Software as a Service (SaaS) apps, and Private Access (ZPA) application segments. Select the Negate checkbox if you want the policy to apply to all destinations except the ones selected.

You can configure application-based forwarding policies that allow the Zero Trust Branch appliance to route traffic only to specific applications. To do this, select a SaaS Apps object from the Destinations drop-down menu. Zscaler provides a list of SaaS apps (e.g., 1Password, Adobe, etc.) that you can use to create a SaaS Apps object. You can define a SaaS Apps object with specific applications based on your requirements.
Add CIDR: Enter the IP address range in CIDR format for the selected destinations. This option appears only if the Subnet/host type destination is selected.

Ports: Select the port category to which this forwarding rule must apply from the drop-down menu. Select the Negate checkbox if you want the policy to apply to all ports except the ones selected. You can select All, Allowed Ports, Custom Port, or any objects created for ports. If you select Custom Port, enter the required ports, and click Add.

Forwarding Method: Select a method (LAN/WAN, Routed Tunnel, ZIA-DTLS, or ZPA) to forward traffic. The ZIA-DTLS option is available only for Zero Trust Branch appliances running version 8.1.2 or later.
Override NAT: Enable this to override the NAT configuration for traffic matching forwarding policy. This option is available only for Zero Trust Branch appliances running version 8.3.0 or later.
Appliance 1: The Zero Trust Branch appliance for the site is filled in automatically.
If the site is running Zero Trust Branch appliances in a cluster, the Appliance 2 section also appears.
Nexthop Interface Type: Select LAN/WAN, ZIA, or ZPA from the drop-down menu. This decides how the traffic should be routed. If you select LAN/WAN, provide the following information:
Primary Interface: Select the primary WAN or LAN interface.
Nexthop IP: Enter the IP address of the primary router or gateway to which the traffic must be routed.
Secondary Interface: Select the secondary WAN or LAN interface.
Nexthop IP: Enter the IP address of the secondary router or gateway to which the traffic must be routed.
Traffic Distribution: If WAN is selected as both primary and secondary interfaces, you can select how you want to balance traffic between the primary and secondary nexthops:
Best: Zero Trust Branch decides programmatically how to distribute traffic.
Balanced: Load is balanced between primary and secondary WANs.
None: The primary interface takes as much load as possible.
Advanced Options:
Match return traffic: Select this option to apply the forwarding policy to return traffic.
Apply for locally generated traffic: Select this option to apply the forwarding policy to traffic originating from the Zero Trust Branch appliance.
See image.
Click Save.
The forwarding policy is created.
Click Commit to apply the changes.
See image.

blocks.text: Based on your requirements, you can edit, reorder, or delete policies and configure routing settings. To learn more, see Managing Forwarding Policies.
